name: IS42S16400J-7TLI
title: 64 Mbit (4M x 16, four banks) 3.3 V synchronous DRAM
summary: A 64 Mbit SDRAM arranged as four banks of 1M words by 16 bits, on a single 3.3 V supply with LVTTL inputs and outputs. Every signal is taken on the rising clock edge; bursts of 1, 2, 4, 8 or a full page, sequential or interleaved, and CAS latency of 2 or 3 are set in a mode register. It has auto refresh (4096 rows per 64 ms, or 16 ms for A2 parts above 85 °C), self refresh, power-down and clock suspend. Speed grades run to 200, 166 and 143 MHz, in 54-pin TSOP II, 54-ball and 60-ball BGA.
key_figures: 143 MHz at CL = 3, 133 MHz at CL = 2

tables.title: Truth table: commands and DQM operation
rows: PRECHARGE (Deactivate row in bank or banks) (5)
AUTO REFRESH or SELF REFRESH (Enter self refresh mode) (6,7)
notes: (1) CKE is HIGH for every command but SELF REFRESH.
(2) The mode-register op-code is taken from A0-A11.
(3) A0-A11 give the row; BA0, BA1 give the bank to open.
(4) A0-A7 give the column and BA0, BA1 the bank. A10 HIGH turns on auto precharge for this one access; A10 LOW leaves it off.
(5) A10 LOW: only the bank on BA0, BA1 is precharged. A10 HIGH: every bank is precharged and BA0, BA1 are ignored.
(6) CKE HIGH gives AUTO REFRESH; CKE LOW gives SELF REFRESH.
(7) Rows are addressed by the internal refresh counter; every input and I/O except CKE is ignored.
(8) DQM enables or disables the DQs: at once during WRITEs, two clocks later during READs.

tables.title: Truth table: CKE
rows: See Truth table: current state bank n, command to bank n
notes: (1) CKEn is the CKE level sampled on edge n, CKEn-1 the level on the previous edge.
(2) Current state means the condition of the device just before edge n.
(3) COMMANDn is registered at edge n; ACTIONn is what it causes.
(4) Any state or sequence not listed is illegal or reserved.
(5) Leaving power-down at edge n leaves all banks idle in time for edge n+1, if tCKS is met.
(6) Leaving self refresh at edge n leaves all banks idle once tXSR has passed. Only COMMAND INHIBIT or NOP may be given during tXSR, and at least two NOPs must be.
(7) After clock suspend ends at edge n, the next command is recognised at edge n+1.

tables.title: Truth table: current state bank n, command to bank n
tables.conditions: CKEn-1 HIGH and CKEn HIGH; tXSR met if the previous state was self refresh
rows: READ (Select column and start READ burst) (10)
WRITE (Select column and start WRITE burst) (10)
PRECHARGE (Deactivate row in bank or banks) (8)
READ (Select column and start new READ burst) (10)
WRITE (Select column and start WRITE burst) (10)
READ (Select column and start READ burst) (10)
WRITE (Select column and start new WRITE burst) (10)
notes: (2) The state is one bank's, and the commands are those that bank may take in it; exceptions are noted.
(3) Idle: the bank is precharged and tRP has passed.
(3) Row Active: a row is open, tRCD has passed, and no burst or register access is under way.
(3) Read: a READ burst without auto precharge has started and has not finished or been cut short.
(3) Write: a WRITE burst without auto precharge has started and has not finished or been cut short.

(4) These states must run to completion without a command to the same bank; give COMMAND INHIBIT, NOP, or a command the other bank allows. Precharging runs from PRECHARGE until tRP. Row Activating runs from ACTIVE until tRCD. Read or Write with auto precharge enabled runs from the command until tRP; each ends with the bank idle or row active as named.

(5) No executable command is accepted in these states; COMMAND INHIBIT or NOP goes on every rising edge. Refreshing runs from AUTO REFRESH until tRC; Accessing Mode Register runs from LOAD MODE REGISTER until tMRD; Precharging All runs from PRECHARGE ALL until tRP. Each ends with all banks idle.
(6) Any state or sequence not listed is illegal or reserved.
(7) Not per bank: every bank must be idle.
(8) Per bank or not; to precharge every bank, each one must be in a state that permits it.
(9) Not per bank: it cuts the latest READ or WRITE burst whichever bank holds it.
(10) Each READ or WRITE row covers both auto precharge on and off.
(11) Acts as a NOP on that bank and leaves its state unchanged.

tables.title: Truth table: current state bank n, command to bank m
tables.conditions: CKEn-1 HIGH and CKEn HIGH; tXSR met if the previous state was self refresh
rows: Any Command Otherwise Allowed to Bank m
READ (Select column and start READ burst) (7)
WRITE (Select column and start WRITE burst) (7)
READ (Select column and start new READ burst) (7,10)
WRITE (Select column and start WRITE burst) (7,11)
READ (Select column and start READ burst) (7,12)
WRITE (Select column and start new WRITE burst) (7,13)
READ (Select column and start new READ burst) (7,8,14)
WRITE (Select column and start WRITE burst) (7,8,15)
READ (Select column and start READ burst) (7,8,16)
WRITE (Select column and start new WRITE burst) (7,8,17)
notes: (2) The state is bank n's; the commands are those bank m may take, given bank m is itself in a state that allows them.
(3) Idle: the bank is precharged and tRP has passed.
(3) Row Active: a row is open, tRCD has passed, and no burst or register access is under way.
(3) Read: a READ burst without auto precharge has started and has not finished or been cut short.
(3) Write: a WRITE burst without auto precharge has started and has not finished or been cut short.
(3) Read or Write with auto precharge enabled runs from the command until tRP, after which the bank is idle.
(4) Every bank must be idle before a refresh command (auto or self) or a mode-register load.
(5) BURST TERMINATE cannot be sent to another bank; it acts only on the bank in the current state.
(6) Any state or sequence not listed is illegal or reserved.
(7) READ and WRITE to bank m cover both auto precharge on and off.
(8) Concurrent auto precharge: bank n starts its auto precharge when bank m's burst cuts into its own.
(9) Bank n's burst carries on as started.
(10) READ on n (no auto precharge) cut by READ on m: the bank m read takes over CAS latency later.
(11) READ on n (no auto precharge) cut by WRITE on m: the write takes over when registered. Raise DQM one clock before the WRITE to avoid bus contention.
(12) WRITE on n (no auto precharge) cut by READ on m: the read takes over when registered, data out CAS latency later; bank n's last written data is the word registered one clock before the READ.
(13) WRITE on n (no auto precharge) cut by WRITE on m: the new write takes over when registered; bank n's last written data is the word registered one clock ahead of the bank m READ.
(14) READ with auto precharge on n cut by READ on m: the bank m read takes over CAS latency later; bank n's precharge starts when the READ to m is registered.

(15) READ with auto precharge on n cut by WRITE on m: the write takes over when registered; raise DQM two clocks before the WRITE to avoid bus contention. Bank n's precharge starts when the WRITE to m is registered.

(16) WRITE with auto precharge on n cut by READ on m: the read takes over when registered, data out CAS latency later. Bank n's precharge starts once tWR has run from the READ to m; its last written data is the word one clock before that READ.

(17) WRITE with auto precharge on n cut by WRITE on m: the new write takes over when registered. Bank n's precharge starts once tWR has run from the WRITE to m; its last written data is the word one clock before that WRITE.
In note 13 the word READ should read WRITE: the second command is a WRITE to bank m.

operation.text: A 67,108,864-bit synchronous DRAM in four banks of 16,777,216 bits. Each bank holds 4,096 rows of 256 columns, each column a 16-bit word. A row is picked by A0-A11 and a bank by BA0, BA1 when ACTIVE is given; the starting column is picked by A0-A7 with READ or WRITE. All inputs are taken on the rising edge of CLK and all levels are LVTTL. A new column address may be given on every clock.

There are three speed grades: -5 (200 MHz at CL = 3), -6 (166 MHz) and -7 (143 MHz). At CL = 2 all three run to 133 MHz. IS42S parts are commercial and industrial grades; IS45S parts are automotive A1 (-40 to +85 °C) and A2 (-40 to +105 °C).

Apply VDD and VDDQ together, run the clock stable, and hold DQM and CKE HIGH. Wait at least 100 µs, giving only COMMAND INHIBIT or NOP meanwhile (at least one of them). Then PRECHARGE all banks, wait tRP, give two or more AUTO REFRESH commands each tRC apart, and load the mode register, whose state at power-up is unknown. After LOAD MODE REGISTER at least one NOP must come before the next command, and tMRD must pass before ACTIVE. The mode register may also be loaded before the refresh cycles. Memory operation starts 200 µs after VDD and VDDQ reach their specified levels.

Loaded from A0-A11 by LOAD MODE REGISTER, only with all banks idle, and kept until loaded again or power is lost. M0-M2 set burst length (1, 2, 4, 8, or full page for sequential bursts), M3 the burst type, M4-M6 the CAS latency (2 or 3), M7-M8 the operating mode (both 0 for normal operation), M9 the write burst mode; M10-M11 are reserved. Reserved codes and test modes give undefined behaviour.

A READ or WRITE selects a block of columns the size of the burst length, and the burst wraps inside that block. The block is chosen by A1-A7 for a burst of 2, A2-A7 for 4 and A3-A7 for 8; the lower bits give the first column. Sequential or interleaved order is set by M3. A full-page burst runs through all 256 columns of the row and wraps until stopped by BURST TERMINATE or PRECHARGE; it is used to build bursts of any length.

With a READ registered on edge n and latency m, the DQs start driving after edge n + m - 1 and the data is valid by edge n + m, provided tAC is met. CL = 2 allows up to 133 MHz on every grade; CL = 3 allows 200, 166 or 143 MHz on the -5, -6 and -7.

ACTIVE opens one row in one bank; READ and WRITE may follow after tRCD. The row stays open until that bank is precharged. A second ACTIVE to the same bank needs the row closed first and tRC between the two ACTIVEs; an ACTIVE to another bank may be given while the first is busy, at least tRRD later, which hides row overhead.

Data from the first column appears CAS latency after READ, and a new word follows on each clock. When the burst ends with no further command the DQs return to high impedance. A new READ, to any bank, may be given on any clock and cuts the burst; issue it CL - 1 clocks before the last wanted word to keep the data continuous. No 2n prefetch rule applies. A READ may also be cut by WRITE: hold DQM HIGH for at least three clocks before the WRITE to silence the read data (output masking lags DQM by two clocks), and leave at least one idle cycle if the other driver can turn on before the SDRAM turns off. PRECHARGE or BURST TERMINATE given CL - 1 clocks before the last wanted word ends a read; after PRECHARGE the bank needs tRP before its next command.

The first word is taken on the same edge as the WRITE and one word on each following edge. After a fixed burst, further input is ignored. A new WRITE or a READ may be given on any clock and takes over; once a READ is registered, input data is ignored. To end a write with PRECHARGE, give it tWR after the last wanted word and mask with DQM the edge before and the edge of the PRECHARGE. With BURST TERMINATE, the word on the terminate edge is not written; the last word written is the one a clock earlier. With auto precharge, tWR is never less than one clock plus a fixed time, whatever the frequency.

DQML masks DQ0-DQ7 and DQMH masks DQ8-DQ15. On a read, a mask raised on one edge puts that byte in high impedance two clocks later; on a write, a mask raised on an edge stops that byte being written on the same edge.

PRECHARGE closes the open row in one bank (A10 LOW, bank on BA0, BA1) or in all banks (A10 HIGH, BA0, BA1 ignored); the bank may be opened again tRP later. Auto precharge, chosen per command with A10 HIGH on READ or WRITE, closes the row by itself at the earliest valid point after the burst, and does not apply to full-page bursts. A precharge given at the best moment does the same as auto precharge, but needs the command bus free then; in exchange it can cut a burst short.

The device supports concurrent auto precharge: a READ or WRITE to bank m may cut a burst in bank n that has auto precharge on. Bank n's precharge then starts when the new command is registered (bank n was reading) or tWR after it (bank n was writing). If a WRITE cuts a READ, raise DQM two clocks before the WRITE to avoid bus contention.

AUTO REFRESH (CBR) refreshes one row using an internal address counter; address inputs are ignored and nothing else may be done for tRC. 4,096 refreshes are needed in each tREF: 64 ms for commercial, industrial and A1, 16 ms for A2 above 85 °C. AUTO REFRESH and SELF REFRESH require all banks idle.

Given as AUTO REFRESH with CKE taken LOW. The device then refreshes itself with no clock and every input but CKE ignored, for at least tRAS and for as long as CKE stays LOW. To leave, run the clock, raise CKE, and give NOP or COMMAND INHIBIT (at least two NOPs) for tXSR. Because the last row refreshed is unknown, a burst of auto refreshes over all rows should follow at once. Self refresh is not supported on A2 parts above 85 °C.

CKE taken LOW with NOP or COMMAND INHIBIT while no access is running enters power-down: precharge power-down with all banks idle, active power-down with a row open. Input and output buffers other than CKE are switched off. No refresh happens, so the device may stay in power-down no longer than the 64 ms refresh period. NOP or COMMAND INHIBIT with CKE HIGH, meeting tCKS, leaves it.

CKE taken LOW during a burst freezes the internal clock: each edge that samples CKE LOW cancels the next internal edge, commands and input data on it are ignored, output data stays driven and the burst counter holds. CKE HIGH resumes on the following edge.
With M9 = 1, every WRITE writes one column whatever the burst length, while READs still use the programmed length and order.
COMMAND INHIBIT (CS HIGH) blocks new commands without disturbing operations in progress. NOP (CS LOW, RAS, CAS, WE HIGH) keeps unwanted commands out during idle or wait cycles.
